newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PEACE REIGNS IN THE SOUTH AMERICAN QUALIFIERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEACE REIGNS IN THE SOUTH AMERICAN QUALIFIERS.

text.p: Argentina's hopes of reaching next year's World Cup finals in France were greatly enhanced as they beat Ecuador 2-1 on a peaceful night in the South American World Cup qualifiers on Wednesday.

Argentina's win in Buenos Aires lifted them above Bolivia and Ecuador, taking them into third place in the nine-team South American group and back into the qualifying places. The top four teams will go to France.

They also closed the gap on second-placed Colombia to one point after the Colombians suffered a shock 1-0 home defeat against Peru, who revitalised their own campaign. Colombia have 17 points and Argentina 16, both from ten games.
Group leaders Paraguay moved six points clear and look almost certain to qualify after beating two-times champions Uruguay 3-1 in Asuncion.
Uruguay are level on 13 points with Bolivia, Ecuador and Peru, but have the worst goal difference and the most difficult remaining fixtures.
Chile, who beat Venezuela 6-0 on Tuesday with Ivan Zamorano scoring five, have 12 points but with five home fixtures left could sneak in.

Despite two sendings-off in Asuncion and one in the Colombia-Peru game in Barranquilla, there was no repitition of the shocking scenes which marred the Bolivia-Argentina and Paraguay-Colombia games earlier this month.
World soccer's governing body FIFA announced their sanctions on Tuesday and many may feel that Argentina, who were the main protagonists, got off extremly lightly.

Goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez and midfielder Gustavo Zapata were suspended for three games each and defender Nelson Vivas for one -- the first for head-butting an opponent and the latter two for being sent off. None are key players.

Yet nearly the entire Argentine team were invovled in a brawl with members of the Bolivia team bench and police which held up play for ten minutes near the end of the game. At least one player was seen spitting in the direction of Bolivian fans.
Ironcially, Argentines were even celebrating because they will not have to face Paraguayan goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert when they travel to Asuncion in July.
Chilavert scored from a free kick as Paraguay drew their first match with Argentina in Buenos Aires last year and his mere presence on the field seemed to psyche out the Argentine team.
But on Tuesday, he received a four-match suspension for his part in the brawl in the Colombia game in Asuncion -- a decision that seemed harsh when compared to Gonzalez's ban.
Argentina's campaign in the qualifiers has been fitful and on Wednesday they gave another stuttering performance.
They began well, racing into a 2-0 lead with goals by Ariel Ortega and Hernan Crespo in the first 32 minutes, but then fell to pieces.

Ortega, Argentina's star player, was continually outshone by his rival number ten Alex Aguinaga as Ecuador, who had won their last two meetings with Argentina, fought their way back into the game. Crespo, despite his goal, failed to justify his inclusion at the expense of out-of-favour Gabriel Batistuta.
Aguinaga pulled a goal back in the 67th minute and then lanky striker Eduardo Hurtado missed two good chances to equalise for Ecuador, who are aiming to go to the World Cup for the first time.
Ecuador's poor away form, where they have only one point from a possible 12, could be their undoing.
Paraguay, backed by a delirious 45,000 crowd, made light of Chilavert's absence as they won with goals by Aristides Rojas, Derlis Soto and Jose Cardozo, who scored from a penalty.
Colombia striker Faustino Asprilla served the first of a two-match suspension imposed after he was sent off for fighting with Chilavert and he was sorely missed in Barranquilla.
Colombia were never allowed to settle by Peru and lost out to a spectacular 61st minute goal by Jose Pereda.

Pereda fired the ball in from 25 metres after Colombia goalkeeper Farid Mondragon threw the ball straight to him. Mondragon had already been heavily criticised for mistakes in previous games against Paraguay and Argentina.
